Save a pheatmap Objects generated from RGenEDA to File

Source: R/GenSave.R
GenSave.Rd

Saves a pheatmap derived RGenEDA heatmap object to a file in various formats including PNG, JPEG, TIFF, BMP, PDF, and SVG.

Usage

GenSave(
  pheatmap_obj,
  filename,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  units = "in",
  res = 300,
  ...
)

Arguments

pheatmap_obj

A pheatmap object returned by an RGenEDA or pheatmap function.

filename

Character string specifying the path and filename where the heatmap should be saved.

width

Numeric, the width of the output image. Default is 8.

height

Numeric, the height of the output image. Default is 6.

units

Character, units for width and height: one of "in", "cm", "mm", or "px". Default is "in". Values are converted to inches for PDF and SVG output.

res

Numeric, the resolution (in dpi) for raster images. Default is 300.

...

Additional arguments passed to the graphics device function.

Value

Invisibly returns the filename of the saved heatmap.

Details

This function is similar in spirit to ggsave() but works specifically with pheatmap objects.

Examples

data(Snail1KO)
counts <- as.matrix(Snail1KO$rawCounts)
counts <- counts[rowSums(counts >= 10) >= 3, ]
meta <- Snail1KO$metadata
rownames(meta) <- meta$Sample
norm <- log2(t(t(counts) / colSums(counts)) * 1e6 + 1)
obj <- GenEDA(normalized = norm, metadata = meta, counts = counts)
dists <- PlotDistances(obj, meta_cols = "Genotype")
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
GenSave(dists, out, width = 6, height = 5)
file.exists(out)
#> [1] TRUE
